text:
Mira Patel: hey team, first day! on an M2 mac, running into weird path/shim issues with asdf + brew + pyenv. installed brew under /opt/homebrew, installed asdf via brew, but `python` and `node` keep resolving to system versions. any quick checklist? :wave:
DevX Bot: welcome Mira! See onboarding doc https://redwood.dev/onboard. If you paste `which python` + `which node` we can triage faster.
Mira Patel: thanks! output: `which python` -> /usr/bin/python3, `which node` -> /usr/local/bin/node, `echo $PATH` -> /usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:~/.asdf/shims
Samir: probably PATH order. On mac with Homebrew (arm) you want /opt/homebrew/bin early. Also asdf shims need to be before system bins. Try prepending these to your shell rc: 
```
# ~/.zshrc (or ~/.bashrc)
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
```
Luca R.: if you installed asdf via brew the libexec path may be different on some setups. Run `brew --prefix asdf` to check. Also add the asdf completions if you use zsh: `fpath+=$(brew --prefix asdf)/share/zsh/site-functions`
Mira Patel: ok did that, restarted shell, now `which python` -> ~/.asdf/shims/python but `python --version` still 3.8 (we want 3.11).
Samir: make sure you added python plugin and installed version, then `asdf global python 3.11.4` (or the pinned version in our dotfiles). Commands: 
```
asdf plugin-add python
asdf install python 3.11.4
asdf global python 3.11.4
asdf reshim
```
Kate: For node we use asdf-nodejs plugin and we pin in repo .tool-versions. Node's plugin sometimes needs the keyring import step on mac: run `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` before installing if the install fails. Also check you don't have NVM in your rc — NVM prepends its own shims and can conflict.
Mira Patel: found a stray `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh` in my .zshrc from earlier. removed it, reshim, `node -v` now shows v18.16.0 (good). thanks! :thumbsup:
Luca R.: nice. If you still see occasional mismatch, check `asdf which python` and `asdf which node` to see which binary asdf points to. For editor integrations (VS Code) ensure your PATH is loaded in the editor — we recommend launching code from the terminal (`code .`) so it inherits shell env.
Mira Patel: one last Q — where do I find our dotfiles? need to pull company defaults (git config, core.autocrlf, pre-commit hooks).
Samir: repo is at https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles — clone and run `./setup.sh`. It will symlink and add git hooks. If you want a quick apply: `git clone <repo> ~/dotfiles && cd ~/dotfiles && ./setup.sh`
Mira Patel: cloning now. thanks everyone, tagging @luca if any post-setup follow-ups.
Luca R.: ping me if the setup script fails on your shell. Happy first day! :tada:
